matter.MatterTitle: An ordinance approving a host venue agreement between the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County and Competitor Group, Inc. for the Rock ‘n’ Roll Running Series branded road running race.

text:
..title
An ordinance approving a host venue agreement between the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County and Competitor Group, Inc. for the Rock ‘n’ Roll Running Series branded road running race. 
..body
WHEREAS, Competitor Group, Inc. agrees to be responsible for operating a Rock ‘n’ Roll Running Series branded road running race in Nashville and performing certain administrative, operational, and sales and marketing functions related to the race; and,
WHEREAS, Competitor Group, Inc. has agreed to reimburse the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County as it relates to law enforcement and fire service providers, up to Three Hundred Thousand Dollars ($300,000) per event; and,
WHEREAS, the agreement (the “Agreement”) attached to this ordinance as Exhibit 1 sets forth the rights, duties, and obligations of the Metropolitan Government and Competitor Group, Inc. with respect to the annual Rock ‘n’ Roll Running Series branded road running race; and,  
WHEREAS, it is in the best interest of the citizens of Nashville and Davidson County to approve the Agreement. 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ENACTED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE METROPOLITAN GOVERNMENT OF NASHVILLE AND DAVIDSON COUNTY:
Section 1. 	That the host venue agreement between the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County and Competitor Group, Inc., attached hereto and incorporated herein, is hereby approved, and the appropriate Metropolitan Government officials are authorized to execute and deliver it.
Section 2.	That amendments to the agreement may be authorized by resolution of the Metropolitan Council.
Section 3.	That this ordinance shall take effect from and after its final passage, the welfare of the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County requiring it.
..Agenda Analysis
Analysis

This ordinance approves a host city agreement between the Metropolitan Government (“Metro”) and Competitor Group, Inc. (“CGI”) relative to a Rock ‘n’ Roll Running Series-branded road running race.

Per the agreement, CGI would be responsible for annually operating a series of running races within Nashville, including a marathon, half marathon, 10K, 5K and 1K. These races would occur on the fourth weekend of April, constituting a single event.

CGI would provide certain sales, marketing and administrative functions related to the event. No payments from Metro to CGI are required by this agreement. Metro would assist CGI in identifying, applying for, and securing all necessary permits to hold the event. Metro would also coordinate with the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department and the Nashville Fire Department to help safely conduct the event. Metro would also provide pedestrian movement plans, wayfinding signage, and clear access to existing pedestrian bridge. CGI would reimburse Metro up to $300,000 per event for the services provided by law enforcement and fire service providers.

The agreement provides that CGI would indemnify and hold harmless Metro for any claims arising from the negligent or intentional acts or omissions of CGI in connection with this agreement. CGI shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with coverage no less than $2,000,000 and aggregate coverage of no less than $5,000,000.

The agreement term would begin on the date that the contract is approved by all required parties and filed with the Metropolitan Clerk’s Office and end on May 27, 2031. Future amendments to this legislation may be approved by resolution.

Fiscal Note: Metropolitan Government will provide host support services to Competitor Group, Inc. (“CGI”) for the annual event Rock ‘n’ Roll Nashville. Host support services include assistance with approvals and permits, law enforcement and emergency services, and pedestrian movement. CGI will reimburse Metropolitan Nashville Police Department and Nashville Fire Department for law enforcement and emergency services for the event up to $300,000 annually.
